stories.title: New York City’s Next Multifamily Shortage? Buildings to Buy.
stories.excerpt: For years, nearly every conversation about New York City multifamily has centered around one shortage: housing. We don’t have enough apartments. We don’t build fast enough. Vacancy remains tight, construction is expensive, and the regulatory environment makes adding new supply increasingly difficult. But there is another shortage developing that investors and owners should be paying close attention to: a shortage of multifamily buildings to buy. I am talking about quality buildings worth buying — free-market apartment buildings with minimal regulatory risk hurdles. Lev Mavashev. PHOTO: Courtesy Alpha Realty That may sound strange after several years when buyers had the upper hand and plenty of owners struggled to get their pricing. But the market is changing. Capital is coming back faster than quality inventory is coming to market, and the numbers are starting to reflect that. According to Alpha Realty’s second-quarter 2026 multifamily market report, New York City recorded 304 multifamily transactions during the three months ended June 30, up 10.5 percent from the first quarter and 2.4 percent year-over-year. That followed 275 transactions in the first quarter, which itself was up nearly 20 percent from the prior year. In other words, despite elevated borrowing costs, transaction velocity continues to improve. Most of the multifamily transactions have been for free-market and newer construction buildings. What’s interesting is that multifamily buildings with 20-plus units accounted for 112 transactions in the second quarter, up 24.4 percent from the quarter before and 8.7 percent from a year earlier. Those assets represented $872.2 million, or roughly 57 percent of all New York City multifamily dollar volume during the quarter. That follows an already strong first quarter, when properties with at least 20 units accounted for $1.06 billion, or approximately 61 percent of citywide multifamily volume. bullets: NYC multifamily transactions up 10.5% Q1–Q2 2026, 304 deals in Q2.
Capital returning faster than quality free-market inventory reaching market.
Tight supply of buyable buildings with minimal regulatory hurdles emerging.
stories.summary: New York City multifamily transaction volume rebounded in Q2 2026 to 304 deals, up 10.5% QoQ and 2.4% YoY, signaling a shift in market dynamics. However, the real constraint is no longer buyer appetite but scarcity of quality, free-market apartment buildings worth acquiring. Capital is flowing back into the market faster than premium inventory is being listed, creating a seller-favorable environment for owners of well-positioned assets.
stories.impact: In Manhattan and outer-borough submarkets, reduced inventory of tradeable multifamily buildings will compress cap rates and inflate basis for new acquisitions, making ground-up development or conversion more competitive relative to portfolio buys. Developers with entitled land pipelines have a structural advantage; opportunistic sellers should accelerate listings before buyer competition intensifies further. This tightness also signals strong underlying demand absorption and rent resilience supporting development feasibility.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs to Acquire LCN Capital Partners, Expanding Sale-Leaseback Presence
stories.excerpt: Goldman Sachs said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire LCN Capital Partners, a leading investment manager specializing in the sale-leaseback, build-to-suit, and triple-net lease sectors of the real estate market, in a deal valued at up to $410 million. LCN has approximately $3 billion in assets under supervision as of June 30, 2026, primarily from institutions, insurers, and high-net-worth individuals. “LCN’s differentiated platform is highly attractive for our Asset & Wealth Management clients who want diversified sources of returns and offers corporate clients innovative capital solutions,” said David M. Solomon, chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs. “Their focus complements our private real estate team’s broad 30-year track record and will expand our ability to serve our insurance, institutional, and wealth client segments.” LCN originates, negotiates, invests in and manages sale-leaseback, BTS and net lease investments across North America and Europe. Founded in 2011 by Edward V. LaPuma and Bryan York Colwell, New York-based LCN has raised 10 investment funds that aim to outperform credit and real estate alternatives. “Our team, our strategy, and our commitment to our partners, both capital and corporate, remain unchanged — what changes is the scale of our ambition,” said LaPuma. “By combining LCN’s origination network and investment discipline with Goldman Sachs’ unrivaled corporate relationships, global distribution, and client experience teams, we can better serve our investing and tenant partners at a scale no independent firm could match — and become an industry leading platform in triple net lease investing.” The acquisition occurs against a backdrop of significant global market opportunity for investment into sale-leasebacks, with an estimated $14 trillion of corporate-owned property on corporate balance sheets in North America and Europe alone. bullets: Goldman Sachs acquires LCN Capital Partners for up to $410M.
LCN manages $3B AUM in sale-leaseback, build-to-suit, triple-net lease.
Deal expands GS institutional investor access to alternative real estate returns.
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs agreed to acquire LCN Capital Partners, a $3 billion asset manager specializing in sale-leaseback, build-to-suit, and net lease transactions across North America and Europe, for up to $410 million. The deal strengthens Goldman's private real estate platform and its ability to serve institutional, insurance, and wealth clients seeking diversified CRE returns. LCN's focus on origination and capital solutions complements Goldman's 30-year real estate track record.
stories.impact: Consolidation of sale-leaseback and BTS origination platforms under major investment banks increases institutional capital availability and pricing competition for corporate real estate solutions, potentially lowering execution costs for multifamily developers pursuing BTS structures with end-user tenants or build-to-suit arrangements. However, tighter underwriting and higher capital-provider expectations may raise feasibility hurdles on marginal deals.

stories.title: AI-Searched Public Records Alone Insufficient for Title Decision-Making: Study
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-only searches of public records aren’t enough to provide reliable title decision-making at scale, according to a new study by DataTrace, a national provider of property and ownership data and title automation solutions. The company’s analysis, “AI Title Search Tested in the Real World: What Accuracy, Risk and Readiness Really Look Like,” compares AI-only with title plant-supported searches to evaluate completeness, accuracy and insurability. (A title plant is an index of all of the recorded events that affect a property, unique in that it’s posted, or indexed, as the official legal description of the property.) “The study is a projection of potential risk, and the opportunity to look at specific — what we would call, gaps — where the AI solution alone was used,” said Annette Cotton, senior vice president and chief data officer at DataTrace. “It predicts if that property had been insured upon, for instance, what could have been an outcome in terms of not being able to report on, address, or remediate that gap. “Our analysis demonstrates that AI performs best when it operates on a foundation of structured, validated title data, rather than fragmented county-level public records. The speed of AI creates value, but only when paired with the confidence, completeness and accuracy needed for insurable title decisioning. The future isn’t AI versus title professionals. It’s AI powered by trusted title data and guided by experienced title experts. That’s how the industry scales automation without sacrificing confidence or insurability.” DataTrace manages more than 2,000 title plants nationally. The new study is a follow-up to DataTrace’s first white paper on its position concerning title plant value, said Cotton. “This was intended to try to answer more details about that and what the impact would have been based on those early findings when we were doing the AI testing against traditional examination.” Among the current study’s
bullets: DataTrace study: AI-only title searches insufficient for reliable underwriting.
AI performs best on structured data; gaps emerge without title plant support.
Title insurance insurability at risk if AI-only results used for decision-making.
stories.summary: A DataTrace study comparing AI-only versus title plant-supported property searches found that artificial intelligence alone cannot reliably support title decisions at scale. AI performs best when operating on a foundation of structured, valid data; without traditional title plant indexing, gaps emerge that could render properties uninsurable or create title defects. The analysis flags specific risks if properties were insured based solely on AI-generated reports.
stories.impact: Multifamily developers and acquirers relying on automated title platforms for fast underwriting face hidden title and insurability risk; traditional title plants remain essential infrastructure. Delays and costs tied to remediation of AI-missed defects could slow closing timelines and increase holdback reserves, particularly for smaller or non-institutional acquisitions where title quality varies. This reinforces the value of hybrid human-AI title workflows.

stories.title: SFR Leasing Operating System Boom Secures $15M Series A Funding
stories.excerpt: Boom, a leasing operating system for single family rentals (SFR), announced Tuesday that it has secured $15 million in Series A funding. The company also announced the launch of BoomCRM, an agentic leasing and touring customer relationship management product built on top of the Boom’s existing underwriting engine. S3 Ventures led the round, with Mischief VC (fund of Plaid CEO Zach Perret) participating. Repeat participation came from venture capital firms Starting Line VC, Company Ventures, and Gilgamesh Ventures. Founded in 2020 and based in Austin, Texas, Boom bills itself as a financial services infrastructure company for rental operations. It works with property management systems dealing with on-time payments, fraud reduction and revenue growth across the renter lifecycle for SFR, scattered site and manufactured housing (MH) sectors. “We have been fairly conservative to date on the capital we’ve raised and the capital we’ve spent,” said Rob Whiting, CEO and co-founder at Boom. “We have a strong product market fit and have grown about 8x up until our Series A, and we’ve further grown 3x since the start of the year. This funding will help us accelerate several things, including the launch of this product and several more products after this, as well as growing the engineering team to support that, along with go-to-market efforts. As we primarily play in single-family rentals and manufactured housing, we want to continue to double down in those areas.” Boom’s existing products are BoomReport, automated rent reporting to incentivize on-time payments, grow revenue, and build resident credit, and BoomScreen, a tenant screening tool to mitigate fraud, increase leasing velocity, and move in best-qualified renters. Whiting said that most leasing CRMs today are either built multifamily-first or are general-purpose tools such as Salesforce and HubSpot, retrofitted for rentals. bullets: Boom SFR leasing OS raises $15M Series A led by S3 Ventures.
8x growth pre-Series A, 3x growth post-announcement; 3x expansion of user base.
BoomCRM agentic AI product targets leasing, touring, fraud reduction for SFR.
stories.summary: Boom, an Austin-based leasing operating system for single-family rentals, closed a $15 million Series A funding round led by S3 Ventures with participation from Mischief VC and repeat backers. The company has grown 8x to Series A and tripled again since the announcement. Boom launched BoomCRM, an agentic AI CRM product layered on its existing underwriting engine to improve leasing, fraud reduction, and revenue across the renter lifecycle.
stories.impact: Venture capital momentum behind SFR tech platforms signals ongoing investor conviction in fragmented SFR asset classes as an alternative to institutional multifamily, particularly for single-operator and mid-sized portfolios. Proliferation of agentic AI leasing tools will compress operating margins and tenant acquisition costs across the SFR sector, not directly affecting multifamily but indicating competitive pressure on rent growth and pricing for small-unit, scattered-site portfolios.

stories.title: Vantage Data Centers, Nebius Partner on AI Infrastructure at South Wales Campus
stories.excerpt: Denver-based Vantage Data Centers and Amsterdam-based artificial intelligence infrastructure company Nebius announced an agreement to deploy high-density, NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure at Vantage’s CWL1 campus in Newport, Wales, one of Europe’s largest data center campuses. The deployment represents the first announced commercial capacity commitment in the South Wales AI Growth Zone and will support growing UK demand for domestic AI compute capacity. Under the agreement, Nebius will lease high-density capacity at CWL1 to support AI training, inference, agentic AI and enterprise AI workloads, serving enterprises, researchers, startups and public sector organizations seeking access to advanced AI infrastructure. “This is an important milestone for South Wales and for the UK’s AI infrastructure ambitions,” said David Howson, president, EMEA, Vantage Data Centers. “Nebius is scaling AI cloud infrastructure in the UK at a time when demand for domestic compute capacity continues to accelerate. Vantage’s Newport campus provides the scale, connectivity and operational excellence needed to support that growth, and we’re proud to help establish South Wales as a leading destination for AI investment.” South Wales was designated as a UK AI Growth Zone in recognition of its concentration of digital infrastructure, fiber connectivity to London, high-capacity electricity grid infrastructure and strong industrial base. The region is also home to the UK’s largest cluster of semiconductor businesses. bullets: Vantage Data Centers, Nebius deploy NVIDIA AI infrastructure at CWL1, Wales.
First commercial capacity commitment in UK's South Wales AI Growth Zone.
Lease supports AI training, inference, enterprise workloads for UK/Europe demand.
stories.summary: Vantage Data Centers and Netherlands-based AI infrastructure company Nebius announced an agreement to deploy high-density NVIDIA AI compute capacity at Vantage's CWL1 data center campus in Newport, Wales. The lease represents the first announced commercial commitment in the UK's new South Wales AI Growth Zone and will serve UK and European enterprises, researchers, and public sector organizations seeking domestic AI infrastructure. The deployment supports growing demand for UK-based compute capacity.
stories.impact: Data center development, not multifamily. However, the UK AI Growth Zone designation and infrastructure investment signal policy-driven regional economic development that could spark downstream population and corporate migration into South Wales and surrounding areas, potentially creating future office and multifamily demand in the region if tech talent and services follow. Monitor for secondary effect on Welsh residential and office submarkets.

stories.title: Atrium Launches AI Platform, Tracking $1.3T of U.S. Data Center Development Credit
stories.excerpt: The data center marketplace keeps growing, and one analytics firm has tracked where all $1.3 trillion of identifiable debt powering this development boom of nearly 4,300 U.S. data centers has come from — and where it is going. Commercial Observer can first report that Atrium, a San Diego-based AI analytics startup founded in 2024, has launched its new interactive data and research platform, “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” to track the debt dollars behind every data center deal in the U.S. The platform is a first-of-its-kind resource that uses data collated from local property records, SEC credit agreements, commercial mortgage-backed security (CMBS) securitizations, as well as commercial bank and private credit loan syndications and corporate debt issuances to follow the money behind 3,038 operational data center deals — and another 1,258 that are in different stages of their lifecycles. Ryan Alfred, founder at Atrium Data, told CO that “data centers are the biggest driver in the economy right now,” but because they’re financed differently than traditional real estate classes — and often require layers of county-level loans, syndicated debt, CMBS, asset-backed securities, SPV structures, and, most unusually, credit issued by regional utility companies — it has been difficult for market players to get a clear picture on the debt behind the boom. “As a result, no one had this 360-degree view of who is financing them and what their credit structures are,” he said. “We went out and used all our data, and all our resources, to build the 360-degree vehicle of data center financings.” The firm’s website notes that the tool and report are “the first in an ongoing series that will track every identifiable data center investment dollar in the United States” and that it will be updated periodically as deals close, including securitizations and county-level recordings. bullets: Atrium launches AI platform tracking $1.3T U.S. data center development debt.

stories.summary: Atrium, a San Diego-based AI analytics startup founded in 2024, launched "Who Finances America's Data Centers," an interactive platform tracking $1.3 trillion in identifiable debt financing 4,300+ U.S. data centers. The platform consolidates data from property records, SEC filings, CMBS securitizations, bank loans, and syndications to map capital flows behind 3,038 operational and 1,258 in-development data center deals. It offers a first-of-its-kind view of data center financing sources and destinations.
stories.impact: Data center financing, not multifamily. However, the massive debt concentration in data center development ($1.3T) signals continued capital reallocation away from traditional office and toward AI infrastructure, compressing CRE debt markets and raising borrowing costs for non-AI-adjacent assets. Multifamily developers competing for institutional debt in tight capital markets will face stiffer pricing as lenders chase higher-risk, higher-yield data center deals.

stories.title: Corpay’s Cross-Border Business Leases Prebuilt at Rudin’s 560 Lexington
stories.excerpt: Rudin announced a new 11-year office lease with Corpay, Inc.’s. Cross-Border business at 560 Lexington Ave., its 22-story office tower in the Plaza District. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which specializes in foreign exchange, global payments and risk management, will relocate its headquarters to 560 Lexington this fall. The company will occupy a 17,778-square-foot prebuilt space spanning the entire 17th floor of the 380,000-square-foot building. “Corpay’s commitment to 560 Lexington demonstrates the continued allure of the Plaza District and further validates our investments in our portfolio’s amenity and prebuild programs,” said Kevin Daly, VP of office leasing at Rudin. “Given these ongoing efforts, only minor modifications to a prebuilt floor were needed to meet Corpay’s requirements. This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done.” Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay. Rudin was represented in-house by Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. bullets: Corpay Cross-Border leases 17,778 SF prebuilt at 560 Lexington Ave., NYC.

Rudin's prebuilt floor strategy enabled accelerated occupancy and deal close.
stories.summary: Rudin Management Company announced an 11-year office lease with Corpay, Inc.'s Cross-Border Solutions division for 17,778 square feet at 560 Lexington Avenue in the Plaza District. Corpay will relocate its foreign exchange and global payments headquarters to the entire 17th floor this fall. Rudin's prebuilt space and minor-modification approach allowed Corpay to meet an accelerated move-in timeline, citing the Plaza District's continuing appeal for corporate tenants.
stories.impact: Office leasing, not multifamily. However, the lease signals continued corporate confidence in Plaza District (Midtown Manhattan) as a premium office anchor, supporting ongoing employer presence and white-collar job stability in the submarket. This reinforces multifamily demand fundamentals in Midtown East and surrounding residential neighborhoods; sustained office occupancy supports proximate renter bases and stabilizes rental demand for luxury and class-A apartments near the Plaza District.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit multifamily property in West Hollywood. The property sold for $7.98 million, or $266,000 per unit. “The property presented the buyer with a rare opportunity to acquire a well-located West Hollywood asset at an attractive basis with significant value-add potential,” said Tony Azzi, executive managing director investments. “With opportunities to renovate vacant units and improve operations, the buyer is well positioned to enhance the property’s long-term cash flow. West Hollywood continues to benefit from strong rental demand driven by limited housing supply, walkability and access to major employment and lifestyle destinations throughout Los Angeles,” added Rabbie Banafsheha, senior director investments. Azzi and Banafsheha, of The Azzi Group in Marcus & Millichap’s Los Angeles office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller. Azzi, Banafsheha, Arteen Zahiri and Ian Habbestad, also of The Azzi Group, procured the buyer. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closes West Hollywood 30-unit sale at $266K per unit ($7.98M).
Value-add play with unit renovation and operational improvement upside.
West Hollywood supply-constrained; strong demand tied to walkability, employment access.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap's Azzi Group closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit multifamily property in West Hollywood, for $7.98 million ($266,000 per unit). The buyer acquired the asset with significant value-add potential through unit renovations and operational improvements. Azzi Group cited West Hollywood's limited housing supply, walkability, and proximity to major employment and lifestyle centers as drivers of strong rental demand.
stories.impact: West Hollywood remains supply-constrained and rental-demand-resilient, supporting continued basis compression and valuation pressure on value-add acquisitions. Sub-$300K per-unit pricing for 30-unit, non-institutional assets reflects aggressive competition from value-add buyers; developers considering West Hollywood infill projects or conversions face higher residual land costs and tighter development feasibility, especially if renovation scope is large. Scarcity of tradeable supply continues to benefit existing owner-operators.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Debt + Equity team led by Robert Delitsky and Keith Braddish arranged a $75-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of Whitestone Shopping Center, a 119,584-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center located at 153-17 Cross Island Pkwy. in Whitestone, Queens. Northmarq arranged financing on behalf of BTF Whitestone LLC after running a marketing process with the lending community. Northmarq and ownership selected Acadia Realty Trust. The principals of BTF Whitestone LLC are Aaron Malinsky and Kenneth Schuckman. “After being overlooked for decades, Whitestone Shopping Center is about to undergo a significant transformation that will benefit both its tenants and the surrounding community,” said Delitsky. “Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky are the ideal developers to restore Whitestone Shopping Center into a vibrant neighborhood retail destination.” The center is anchored by Key Food Supermarket, with additional tenants including Webster Bank and JPMorgan Chase. The post Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranges $75M acquisition loan for Whitestone Shopping Center, Queens.
119,584 SF grocery-anchored center; Key Food anchor; Acadia Realty lender.
Loan funds acquisition and redevelopment of long-overlooked neighborhood retail asset.
stories.summary: Northmarq arranged a $75 million acquisition and redevelopment loan for Whitestone Shopping Center, a 119,584-square-foot grocery-anchored retail property in Queens, for developer BTF Whitestone LLC. The center is anchored by Key Food Supermarket with additional tenants including Webster Bank and JPMorgan Chase. Acadia Realty Trust provided the financing, which backs a significant redevelopment plan to revitalize a long-neglected neighborhood retail destination.
stories.impact: Retail redevelopment, not multifamily. However, Whitestone, Queens is a value market with emerging redevelopment activity; grocery-anchored centers undergoing capital-intensive repositioning signal neighborhood stabilization and rising consumer traffic. If the Whitestone Shopping Center project succeeds, proximate residential demand and rents could rise, creating a future acquisition or development window for nearby multifamily sites. Monitor Queens neighborhood-anchored retail projects as leading indicators of residential demand recovery in secondary submarkets.

stories.title: Starwood Lands $483M CMBS Loan to Refi Single-Family Rental Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan to refinance a nearly full single-family rental portfolio located across 10 states. The floating-rate, interest-only financing — which Japan’s Nomura Securities originated — backs 1,749 properties, according to Fitch Ratings. The debt, which is scheduled to mature in August 2028, has three 12-month extension options. The portfolio was just over 96 percent leased in April. On average, the homes span 1,812 square feet and date back to 1992. Starwood Asset Management paid $674 million for the houses, assembling the portfolio between 2021 and 2022. Nearly a third are located in Georgia, followed by nearly a quarter in Arizona and just under 12 percent in Florida. Within Palm Beach County, there are 27 homes, most of which are located in Lake Worth, according to property records. The debt comes as Starwood has been making other multifamily inroads, buying four affordable housing properties across Miami-Dade County just last week for a combined $115 million. For Nomura, the financing marks a sizable loan since re-entering the U.S. market last year after a 27-year hiatus. A division of Nomura Group, one of Japan’s major financial institutions, the firm had helped pioneer the CMBS scheme back in the 1990s. Representatives for Starwood declined to comment, while representatives for Nomura did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management secures $482.5M CMBS refi for 1,749-unit SFR portfolio.
Portfolio across 10 states; 96%+ leased; Nomura originated floating-rate debt.
Maturity Aug 2028 with three 12-month extensions; homes span 1,800+ SF.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million CMBS loan (originated by Nomura Securities) to refinance a nearly full 1,749-unit single-family rental portfolio spanning 10 states. The portfolio, assembled between 2021–2022 at a $674 million acquisition cost, was 96%+ leased as of April and comprises homes averaging 1,812 square feet. The floating-rate, interest-only debt matures in August 2028 with three 12-month extension options; 31% of units are in Georgia, 24% in Arizona, and 12% in Florida.
stories.impact: SFR refinancing activity signals continued institutional investor confidence in single-family rental yields and credit, but refinancing (not new acquisition) indicates SFR valuations and debt capacity are stable, not expanding aggressively. High leverage on 1,749 units tied to floating-rate CMBS debt exposes Starwood to rate reset risk and refinance timing risk in a potentially higher-rate environment by Aug 2028; if refi markets tighten, distressed SFR sales could depress rents across Georgia, Arizona, and Florida. Multifamily developers in these markets should monitor SFR distress as a leading indicator of rental market weakness.
